content.text:
I reviewed every input file, all ten draft sections, the numeral ledger, and all seven figure briefs, and built a full limitation-by-limitation ledger against the disclosure.

## Ledger result (summary of tracing)

Traced to affirmative inventor passages: the rail/upper face/lower face/longitudinal slot/printed distance marks; the fixed fence at the first end, its downwardly projecting portion, perpendicularity, and edge bearing; the two-screw/two-hole releasable mounting and the invert-and-reinstall reversal moving the projection to the opposite longitudinal side; the removable parallel-faced spacer plate that changes setback without changing separation; the two separate carriages, keys in the slot preventing rotation while permitting sliding, cylindrical hardened replaceable bushings with bores through the carriage registering with the slot, bores parallel and perpendicular to the lower face; the clamp knob/threaded shank/clamping shoe clamping the rail; the two pointers aligned with their bore axes and the difference-equals-spacing relationship; the transverse center index at the midpoint, the shallow V sight notch in the second end aligned with it, and alignment with a pencil centerline; the full method sequence and lift-away; the rigid-polymer-or-metal material list and the no-motor/battery/sensor/network negative limitations. Claims 1–22 each map to those passages; Background prior-art characterizations were not required to trace.

Two geometry points I checked hard and did **not** flag: the stepped 3-3/5-5 cutting planes (the bore and the knob shank both pass through the same longitudinal slot, so a lengthwise offset is forced by the source, and the briefs never say which is nearer the fence), and FIG. 7's lengthwise centerline alignment (the source itself places the notch at the second end "aligned with the center index" at the midpoint, which forces a lengthwise common alignment).

## Findings (3)

1. **Major** — clamp knobs 58/78 are cited to FIG. 1, but FIG. 1 shows them only as an unlabeled "plain round body" and its numeral list omits both.
2. **Minor** — spacer paragraph contradicts itself about what bears on the edge.
3. **Minor** — FIG. 6 says portion 32 "stands on one longitudinal side of the rail" while the fence is shown lifted off in an exploded view.

input.summary: Full source-fidelity preflight completed. Every claim limitation in claims 1-22, every entry in the numeral ledger (10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 24, 26, 30, 32, 34, 36, 40, 50, 52, 54, 58, 60, 62, 70, 72, 74, 78, 80, 82, 90, 92, 94), every numbered part as used in the description, all seven figure briefs and the Brief Description of the Drawings, the abstract, and the summary were checked and traced item by item against affirmative USER passages in input/disclosure.md and input/conversation.md. The technical substance of the draft traces cleanly: rail with flat lower face, upper face, through-slot and printed distance marks; fixed fence at the first end with downwardly projecting portion, perpendicularity, edge bearing, two-screw/two-hole releasable mounting and the invert-and-reinstall reversal that moves the projection to the opposite longitudinal side while the same marked face is used; removable parallel-faced spacer plate changing setback by its thickness without changing separation; two separate carriages with keys in the slot preventing rotation while permitting sliding; cylindrical hardened replaceable drill bushings whose bores pass completely through the carriage, register with the slot, and are parallel to one another and perpendicular to the lower face; threaded clamp knob, shank through carriage and slot, clamping shoe below the rail clamping the rail between carriage and shoe; two pointers aligned with their bore axes and readable against the same distance marks with the difference equal to center-to-center spacing; transverse center index at the midpoint, shallow V sight notch in the second end aligned with it and with a pencil centerline; the complete method sequence and lift-away with nothing remaining attached; the rigid-polymer-or-metal material list; and the no-motor/no-battery/no-sensor/no-network negative limitations. Background prior-art characterizations were treated as not requiring inventor support. Two geometry points were examined closely and deliberately not reported: the stepped 3-3 and 5-5 cutting planes (a lengthwise offset between bore axis and knob axis is forced because the source has both the bore opening and the knob shank passing through the same longitudinal slot, and the briefs never state which lies nearer the fence), and FIG. 7's lengthwise common alignment of center index, sight notch and centerline (forced by the source statement that the notch at the second end is aligned with the index at the midpoint and that both are aligned with the pencil centerline). Section-line designations 3-3 and 5-5 are used identically in the FIG. 2 source-view brief, the FIG. 3 and FIG. 5 titles, and the Brief Description. No drafting note, placeholder, open question, or unresolved alternative remains. Three defects were verified: one numeral-to-view mismatch where clamp knobs 58 and 78 are cited to FIG. 1 while FIG. 1 depicts them only as an unlabeled round body and omits both numerals from its list, and two minor internal-wording inconsistencies in the spacer-plate use paragraph and the FIG. 6 exploded-view brief. No unsupported invention structure, relationship, material, result, or optional embodiment was found in the claims, description, or figure briefs.

findings.title: Clamp knobs 58 and 78 are cited to FIG. 1 but are neither named nor numbered in the FIG. 1 brief
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md (clamp knob paragraph) and figures/FIG-1.md (body text and "Numerals shown on this figure")
findings.detail: The detailed description twice directs the reader to FIG. 1 for the clamp knobs: "a clamp knob 58 (FIGS. 1 and 5) on the first guide carriage 50 and a clamp knob 78 (FIGS. 1 and 3) on the second guide carriage 70." The FIG. 1 brief, however, never names a clamp knob and lists only "10, 30, 32, 50, 70, 90, 92". The element that would carry those numerals appears in FIG. 1 only as an anonymous shape: "A plain round body, shown schematically, stands above each of the two blocks." The result is that two reference numerals are cited to a view that does not carry them, and FIG. 1 depicts an element that the brief leaves unidentified. The underlying part is source-supported, so the defect is one of labeling, not of fidelity: the disclosure states "Each carriage has a threaded clamp knob above the rail," which is exactly what the round body above each carriage block represents.
findings.evidence: Description: "a clamp knob 58 (FIGS. 1 and 5) on the first guide carriage 50 and a clamp knob 78 (FIGS. 1 and 3) on the second guide carriage 70." | FIG-1.md body: "A plain round body, shown schematically, stands above each of the two blocks." | FIG-1.md numerals: "- 10: rail / - 30: fence / - 32: downwardly projecting portion / - 50: first guide carriage / - 70: second guide carriage / - 90: workpiece / - 92: workpiece edge" (no 58, no 78). | Disclosure: "Each carriage has a threaded clamp knob above the rail."
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-1.md, replace the sentence "A plain round body, shown schematically, stands above each of the two blocks." with "A clamp knob 58 stands above the first guide carriage 50 and a like clamp knob 78 stands above the second guide carriage 70, each shown schematically as a plain round body above the rail 10." and add to the numeral list of FIG. 1: "- 58: clamp knob of the first guide carriage" and "- 78: clamp knob of the second guide carriage". Leave the description citations "(FIGS. 1 and 5)" and "(FIGS. 1 and 3)" unchanged.

findings.title: Spacer-plate use paragraph states that portion 32 is pressed against the edge after the spacer plate is fitted between them
findings.where: draft/08-detailed-description.md, method paragraph beginning "The user marks a centerline 94..."
findings.detail: Within one paragraph the draft first says the downwardly projecting portion 32 is pressed against the workpiece edge 92 after the spacer plate 40 has been interposed between those two parts, and then correctly states the opposite in the next sentence. With the spacer plate fitted, portion 32 bears on the spacer plate and only the spacer plate's outer face touches the edge, as the source and claim 19 both have it. The first sentence is a drafting slip that contradicts the second.
findings.evidence: Description: "Where an increased setback is wanted, the spacer plate 40 is fitted between the downwardly projecting portion 32 and the workpiece edge 92 before the downwardly projecting portion 32 is pressed against that edge. The downwardly projecting portion 32 of the fence 30, or the outer face of the spacer plate 40 when the spacer plate 40 is fitted, is pressed against the selected workpiece edge 92, which fixes the setback." | Disclosure: "presses the fence or the installed spacer plate against the selected workpiece edge" | Claim 19: "pressing the downwardly projecting portion against one of the parallel opposite faces of the spacer plate while the other of the parallel opposite faces bears against the straight edge".
findings.fix: In draft/08-detailed-description.md, replace "before the downwardly projecting portion 32 is pressed against that edge" with "before the jig is pressed against that edge".

findings.title: FIG. 6 brief places portion 32 on a longitudinal side of the rail while showing the fence lifted off the rail
findings.detail: FIG. 6 is an exploded view in which the fence 30 is expressly shown separated from the rail 10, yet the same paragraph states in the present tense that the downwardly projecting portion 32 "stands on one longitudinal side of the rail 10". As written the brief asks the renderer to show the fence both detached and standing on the rail. The relationship itself is source-supported for the installed condition, so only the tense/condition needs correcting.
findings.evidence: FIG-6.md: "The fence 30 is shown lifted off the rail. The fence 30 has a downwardly projecting portion 32 that stands on one longitudinal side of the rail 10." | Disclosure: "Removing the screws, turning the fence over, and reinstalling the screws moves the downwardly projecting part of the fence from one longitudinal side of the rail to the opposite longitudinal side."
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-6.md, replace "The fence 30 has a downwardly projecting portion 32 that stands on one longitudinal side of the rail 10." with "The fence 30 has a downwardly projecting portion 32 that lies on one longitudinal side of the rail 10 when the fence 30 is installed."
